subject: Recap: Performance SLO qualification — Nova Retail
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@novaretail.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-20T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Recap: Performance SLO qualification + next steps

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the call this afternoon. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on SLOs and the levers we'll evaluate: 

High-level targets you mentioned
- Latency: p95 <= 200ms for a 256–512 token response (streaming token-by-token)
- Throughput: ~60k requests/day (~0.7 req/s average, with spikes)
- Peak concurrency: ~80 active concurrent users during flash sales
- Streaming required: yes (token-by-token update to UI)

Key performance/cost levers we discussed (what Redwood can toggle)
- Continuous batching: improves GPU utilization for mid/low-latency SLOs; reduces per-token cost
- Prefix / KV caching: useful if you have repeated prompt prefixes (e.g., product context) to cut repeated compute
- Quantization profiles: rw-medium-q8 and rw-large-q4 options — lower precision reduces latency and memory footprint at small quality cost
- Model variants / routing: can route noise-tolerant requests to a smaller variant; keep the larger model for high-quality or long-context requests
- Autoscaling & dedicated pools: Dedicated capacity for predictable latency during spikes vs hosted bursting for cost savings

What we need from you to run an initial bench and estimate unit economics:
1) Representative prompt set and average/95th prompt length (tokens) — sample payloads are most helpful
2) Expected QPS distribution (e.g., baseline vs peak windows) and concurrency timeline
3) Any hard constraints: strict p95 latency SLA, or acceptable fallbacks (e.g., degrade to non-streaming at tail)

Proposed next steps
- If you can send the sample prompts and a short CSV with QPS/concurrency, Rishi will run a targeted benchmark using: continuous batching on, prefix cache enabled, and a quantized rw-medium-q8 variant. We’ll return: estimated p50/p95 latency, throughput headroom, and per-1M-token cost for the config.
- Tentative tech deep-dive: Wed 2026-12-22 10:00AM PT (30 min) — please confirm availability.

Attaching: performance-runbook.pdf (checklist we’ll follow) and a latency-benchmark template we’ll populate.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole

Marissa —

Thanks for the summary, that matches what we discussed. A few clarifications / data points from our side: 
- Target latency: aiming for p95 <= 180ms for typical 256-token responses in our chat UI (we can tolerate up to 250ms for longer responses)
- Typical prompt size: ~120 tokens; average response length ~220 tokens; worst-case up to ~600 tokens for long-form summaries
- Traffic: current average ~60k req/day, peak QPS ~45 req/s during campaigns for ~10 minute bursts; sustained baseline ~0.8 req/s
- Peak concurrency: 80 (as discussed)
- Streaming: required — UX must show incremental tokens
- Compliance: initial plan is hosted; we may evaluate Dedicated later in Q1 if latency varies during promos

I can share a zip of sample prompts and a CSV with minute-level QPS tomorrow morning. We are available for Wed 12/22 10:00AM PT.

One ask: pls include an estimate for both hosted and dedicated (monthly commit) unit costs, and a quick note on expected degradation modes if we turn on aggressive batching during peaks.
—Sam

1) Hosted, rw-medium-q8, continuous batching ON, prefix cache ON — optimize for cost while hitting p95 180–200ms
